claims.claim: In Python, def introduces a function definition; it is followed by a function name and parenthesized parameter list, and the body begins on the next indented line.
Defining a function associates its name with a user-defined function object; calling the named function later executes its body.
A docstring may be the first statement in a function body, and Python tools can use docstrings to provide documentation.
A named function can package a small behavior so callers can use that behavior repeatedly without duplicating its implementation.
A function call uses parentheses after the function name; a definition and a call are different program actions.
